llm.summary: VRSK outperformed SPY and reached CLEAN_LIFTOFF, with company-specific alpha recorded as the cause. Its watch placement and one-day board tenure suggest recognition before the outcome, but the exact timing mechanism is undocumented.
llm.root_cause: VRSK outperformed SPY and reached CLEAN_LIFTOFF, with company-specific alpha recorded as the cause. Its watch placement and one-day board tenure suggest recognition before the outcome, but the exact timing mechanism is undocumented.
llm.lesson: The company-alpha and watch books surfaced the opportunity, while the timing and catalyst books lack enough evidence to explain why it remained watch rather than buy.
llm.engines_credit: Company-alpha selection is the role model; lane calibration, catalyst attribution, and rotation organs are laggards in evidentiary completeness.

causal_chain.mechanism: Recorded company-specific strength drove relative outperformance.
causal_chain.counterfactual: Without company-specific strength, clean liftoff would be less readily explained.

causal_chain.mechanism: Watch placement after one day on the board may indicate early recognition without full commitment.
causal_chain.counterfactual: Earlier buy classification might have changed participation, but no gate inputs are provided.

causal_chain.mechanism: An unidentified catalyst may have converted the recorded alpha into liftoff.
causal_chain.counterfactual: Without a catalyst, the move might have remained gradual or unrealized.

signal_hypotheses.feature: Residual momentum acceleration among new watch names
signal_hypotheses.measurement: Measure change in market-, sector-, and industry-neutral momentum from board admission using timestamp-safe data.
signal_hypotheses.expected_direction: Positive acceleration should associate with later clean liftoff.
signal_hypotheses.falsifier: Acceleration does not distinguish liftoff from non-liftoff watch outcomes.
